title: Uniform finite Tor bounds for all integral reductions
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $t$ and $A_n=R/t^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $T$ be a separated finite-type scheme over a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, $p\ne\ell$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. On $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ put $\widehat R_T=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$. For any finite list $K^{(1)},\ldots,K^{(s)}$ of objects of the completed integral constructible category $\mathcal I_T(R)$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], write $K^{(i)}_n=K^{(i)}\otimes^L_{\widehat R_T}(A_n)_T$. There exist integers $a\le b$ and a finite locally closed constructible stratification of $T$ such that every $K^{(i)}_n$ has intrinsically constructible cohomology, locally constant with finite $A_n$-module values on those strata [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], and Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ over $(A_n)_T$: for every degree-zero $(A_n)_T$-module sheaf $V$, $H^q(K^{(i)}_n\otimes^L_{(A_n)_T}V)=0$ if $q\notin[a,b]$. The same interval works for all $i,n$, including after restriction to a stratum. More precisely, finitely many pro-etale local trivializations on these strata can be chosen with perfect $R$-complex values $P$ (bounded complexes of finite projective $R$-modules) in degrees $[a,b]$, whose reductions are the finite-projective $A_n$-complexes $P\otimes_R A_n$. Each reduction admits the compatible bounded constructible etale-origin witnesses of the integral category and is therefore in the finite bounded constructible finite-Tor category $D^b_{ctf}(T,A_n)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. The empty list, zero complexes and empty scheme are allowed, with $[0,0]$ when all the complexes are zero.

proof.text: Choose the common interval, stratification and finite perfect scalar charts from lem-pur-integral-finite-perfect-charts. Retain these data unchanged.

Scalar extension preserves finite projective terms. Exact slice restriction computes the reduced homology as the constant sheaf of the finite scalar homology module. Transport through the slice equivalence, and apply finite-model local constancy and stalk finiteness, to obtain intrinsic constructibility on the common strata.

Apply stratified_finite_projective_tor to every termwise scalar quotient complex on the common charts. Additive scalar extension preserves the zero terms outside the fixed interval, giving both global and stratum all-module Tor bounds.

Retain the compatible witnessed tower from membership. Its origins pull back to the reductions through the unit of the canonical coefficient-realization equivalence. Intrinsic constructibility yields constructible etale homology origins; full faithfulness of comparison identifies these with the homology of the retained origins. Tor amplitude gives their cohomological bounds by exact conservative inverse image. Thus the retained origins are bounded constructible. The original normalization equation is copied without modification, and the source bounded-constructible comparison gives constructibleFiniteTor.

The coefficient category is right: 𝓘_T(R) = def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete with the actual completed ring R̂_T = lim(A_n)_T, and K_n is formed as in that definition. No new nodes and no repair note. Steps 1–6 hold. Step 1: characterization (i)⇒(ii); T Noetherian, finite-dimensional, ℓ invertible. Step 2: real fibre-product cones from wide-pullback with U=O_j=T, plus the completed-ring inverse-image comparison and tensor pullback. Step 3: finite qc selection, then min/max of term intervals, fixed before n and V. Step 4: chart tensor comparison with index n−1 and g the stratum immersion; constructibility only from perfect-strata-uniform-reductions. Step 5: projective ⇒ flat ⇒ flat realization ⇒ bounded flat K-flat, so each term vanishes outside [a,b] for arbitrary W. Step 6: exact restriction, tensor pullback and Noetherian stratum detection, also per stratum. Two faults, both repaired in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-smooth-purity/lem-pur-integral-reduction-uniform-tor.json. (1) C4/C2, Step 7: it claimed the witnesses are bounded constructible 'by membership', but the definition gives only L_n ∈ D^+(T_et), and the step was marked elementary. Repaired by citing lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin (ii) (gives C_n ∈ D^b_c(T_et) with ν^*C_n ≅ K_n) and thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison (ν^* fully faithful on D^+, so L_n ≅ C_n). The step is now non-elementary with source BS Def 6.5.1; both nodes are added to proof_deps and declared in split_report.tool_uses; no cycle. (2) B3: the statement names the finite-Tor category without a citation; added [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] to the statement and stmt_deps. Duplicate candidates are not this statement: lem-coef-integral-residue-tor (finite-field datum, no common models), lem-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect and lem-sfb-adic-constructible-finite-reductions (discrete A, single K), perfect-strata-uniform-reductions (cohomological bounds only). Small cases: [R→tR] gives Tor interval [−1,0], also at n=1; shifts; direct sums; empty list or scheme gives [0,0]. No SGA. I accept the 12 declared tool uses.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
